_instructions.DELETE_BEFORE_RETURN: Read input_sources first: the brief may be in _user or in the chat message. Write that many detailed sections (author fields only). Set mode on every section per shot_structure (camera change = t2v, same shot rolling on = continue). Studio composes official H3 three-block prompts. Write logline in English. Invent title if none is given. Check final_checklist, then DELETE _instructions and _user. Return ONLY valid JSON.
_instructions.SIL_SONRA_DON: Konu ve senaryo _user icinde veya sohbet mesajinda olabilir; ikisini de oku, senaryo verildiyse ona sadik kal. N = clip sayisi (varsayilan 12). Her section'a mode yaz: kamera acisi degisiyorsa t2v (kesme), ayni plan suruyorsa continue. Mekan degisince t2v + yeni chapter. Alanlar INGILIZCE ve DETAYLI, diyalog istenen dilde. Sonra _instructions ve _user sil, sadece JSON don.

input_sources.where_the_brief_comes_from: The human gives the brief either in _user (scenes, about) or in the chat message that came with this file, often in Turkish. Use both. If they differ, the chat message wins.
input_sources.scenario_given: If the human describes a scenario or specific events, follow those events in that order and keep their names, places and lines. Only invent what they left open. Do not replace their plot with a different one.
input_sources.topic_only: If the human gives only a topic, invent the whole story from it.
input_sources.scene_count: Use the scene count the human gives (chat or _user.scenes). If the scenario does not fit, keep the count and compress or expand the events.
input_sources.dialogue_language: Dialogue stays in the language the human writes or asks for; set dialogue_lang to its code (tr, en, ...). Every other field is English.
input_sources.no_questions: Do not ask questions back. Deliver the finished JSON in one answer.

language.why: MiniMax H3 still + video prompts must be English. Turkish/other languages in visual fields hurt quality.
write_in_english: characters[].notes, voice, trigger (names may stay as proper nouns)
sections: title, location, character, action, camera, visual_style, audio, music, important, logline
language.dialogue_exception: dialogue may stay in the spoken story language (set dialogue_lang: tr|en|ar|…). Everything else = English.

_instructions.what_this_is: Text-only Character / location (face-lock) package for MiniMax H3 Studio. Human writes clip count + topic only. You write the film. Studio later makes stills + per-clip video (t2v / continue). Studio composes official H3: integrated_multimodal_description / overall_soundscape / non_diegetic_music. No images or URLs from you.

defaults.sections_count: EQUALS _user.scenes (default 12). Add/remove section objects to match.
defaults.total_runtime: 12 clips x 5s = 60s (1 minute). Keep exactly 12 sections unless the user asks otherwise. 3 acts = 36 sections (3 x 12).
defaults.per_section_duration: Optional integer key duration (4-15 seconds) on a section that needs a longer or shorter clip. Omit it to use the Studio duration.
defaults.chapters: Optional key chapter on every section (e.g. Part 1, Part 2). A continue chain never crosses a chapter boundary, so start each chapter with a t2v section and keep the same chapter name on all its sections.
defaults.production_settings: Style, preset, duration, quality, steps and LoRA are selected in Studio and are never part of this JSON.

mode_field.t2v: NEW video — fresh clip (text-to-video / new beat). Use for shot 1 and for every cut: a new camera angle or framing, a new location, a time jump, or a different cast with no overlap.
mode_field.continue: CONTINUE the previous clip seamlessly (Continuum chain: motion tail + the same character/location references). Use when the same beat continues in the same location with overlapping cast. A chain runs from a t2v section through the following continue sections and ends at the next t2v section or chapter change.
mode_field.default_in_this_template: Placeholder modes follow shot_structure.rhythm (t2v, then 1-3 continue, then a new t2v). Set every section's mode from the shots you write.
mode_field.continue_rules: A continue section stays in the same location as the previous section, and its opening_frame should match the previous ending_frame.

how_pipeline_works: 1) Read input_sources: brief from _user and/or the chat message. Invent only what is missing. Visual fields ENGLISH.
2) Write exactly that many detailed author-field sections. Follow shot_structure: every camera change or new location is t2v; the same shot rolling on is continue.
3) User imports. Studio composes the official 3-block H3 prompt per clip. Nothing generates yet.

4) User clicks Produce: stills for cards without images, then scene videos. Each t2v section starts fresh with face lock; following continue sections render as one Continuum chain until the next t2v section or chapter change.
5) No portraits/urls/base64 from you. No integrated_multimodal_description key in the JSON.

field_guide.title: Short section title (optional).
field_guide.location: Place name — must match a locations[].name when possible.
field_guide.character: Who is on screen — match characters[].name (comma-separate if multiple).
field_guide.action: ENGLISH. THIS 5s clip only. 2-5 present-tense visible sentences: body, hands, eyes, props, weather, light. Not a theme. Not one verb.
field_guide.dialogue: Spoken lines in THIS clip only. Empty if silent. May stay in the story language; set dialogue_lang. Do not force a language unless the story needs it.
field_guide.dialogue_lang: auto | tr | en | ar | … — language of dialogue; auto keeps text as written.
field_guide.camera: ENGLISH. On t2v: shot size + height + lens feel + move. On continue: how the SAME shot keeps moving; no new angle. Angles vary only across t2v cuts.
field_guide.visual_style: ENGLISH. Look for THIS clip if it differs from setup; else leave empty to inherit.
field_guide.audio: ENGLISH. Diegetic only. Becomes overall_soundscape. No BGM.
field_guide.music: N/A unless the user asked for score. Becomes non_diegetic_music.
field_guide.important: Must-lock details (costume, prop, continuity). Keep short.
field_guide.reference_subjects: Exact subject names and reference roles.
field_guide.reference_environment: Exact location name and reference role.
field_guide.opening_frame: Visible composition at the beginning of this clip. On continue it equals the previous ending_frame.
field_guide.ending_frame: Visible composition at the end of this clip; the next continue section starts from it.
field_guide.camera_movement: Choose static, push in, pull out, zoom in, zoom out, pan left, pan right, tilt up, tilt down, truck left, truck right, pedestal up, pedestal down, arc or tracking.
field_guide.camera_amplitude: small, large, or empty for normal.
field_guide.camera_speed: slow, fast, or empty for normal.
field_guide.camera_target: Subject toward which the camera moves.
field_guide.transition: hard cut or reverse angle on t2v; continuous on continue.
field_guide.beats: Timed visible beats at 0s, 2s and 4s; consistent with action.

strict_section_contract.why: Studio does NOT guess character or location calls from prose inside prompt/action. It binds cards only from the exact section keys below.
asset_binding: location MUST be the exact name of one entry in locations[].name whenever a named place is visible. Example: location: Alex's Attic Apartment.
character MUST be the exact name of one or more entries in characters[].name whenever a named person is visible. Multiple people: Alex, Maya.
Visible creatures and vehicles also go in character with their exact creatures[].name / vehicles[].name. Example: Kael, IRON REQUIEM, THRESHER.
List at most 8 named assets in one section; each section receives at most 9 reference images in total.
Do not leave location or character blank when a named place/person appears. Empty character is allowed only for a true no-character establishing shot.
Repeat the exact same spelling in every section. Do not use pronouns, roles, shortened names, or descriptions as a substitute for the card name.

canonical_section_example.title: Alex finds the mirror
canonical_section_example.action: Alex steps toward the dusty mirror and slowly raises one gloved hand. His reflection hesitates a fraction behind him while warm attic dust drifts through the window light.
canonical_section_example.camera: Medium close-up at eye level, slow dolly forward toward Alex and the mirror.
canonical_section_example.opening_frame: Medium shot at eye level: Alex in the attic doorway, the dusty mirror on the right.
canonical_section_example.ending_frame: Medium close-up: Alex's gloved hand raised toward the mirror, his reflection a beat behind.
canonical_section_example.audio: Quiet attic room tone, floorboard creak, a faint glass hum.
canonical_section_example.important: Keep Alex's oversized kitchen gloves, towel cape, and swim goggles identical.

forbidden_alternatives: Do NOT use prompt instead of action.
Do NOT use camera_description instead of camera.
Do NOT use video_type; use mode with exactly t2v or continue.
Do NOT use duration_seconds, timecode_start, timecode_end, scene_name, cast, setting, or free-text-only sections.
Do NOT expect Studio to extract names from a long prompt. Put the names explicitly in character and location.

cast_guide.characters: name + ENGLISH notes ONLY (appearance, age, wardrobe — this is the still prompt). Optional English voice tag. trigger = same as name. Leave lora_id empty. Do NOT add image/url fields.
cast_guide.locations: name + ENGLISH notes (architecture, time of day, weather). Notes become the location still prompt.
cast_guide.creatures: name + ENGLISH notes (anatomy, scale, color). Notes become the creature still prompt. No voice/lora. For giants, state scale against the setting (e.g. skyscrapers reach its hips) and keep small objects out of the foreground of their shots so the giant does not read as a toy.
cast_guide.vehicles: name + ENGLISH notes (shape, size, materials, markings). Notes become the vehicle still prompt. Name vehicles in section character like a cast member.

rules: The brief comes from _user and/or the chat message (see input_sources). Do not ask more questions.
Write ALL visual fields in English. Dialogue may stay in the spoken language.

Fill author fields in DETAIL. Follow strict_section_contract exactly: every relevant section must explicitly bind its character and location. Studio composes the official 3-block H3 prompt; production settings stay in the Studio UI.
Do NOT write integrated_multimodal_description / overall_soundscape / non_diegetic_music keys.
TEXT ONLY — no images/URLs/base64. Studio creates stills from name+notes.

human_writes_only.scenes: Integer = how many 5s clips. Default 12 (one minute). Modes follow shot_structure.
human_writes_only.about: Topic or full scenario, in _user.about or in the chat message. Turkish OK; YOU write the visual fields in English. Dialogue stays in the story language.

h3_prompt_format.do_not_write_the_three_blocks: Studio composes the official H3 prompt from author fields. Do NOT output integrated_multimodal_description / overall_soundscape / non_diegetic_music yourself. Do NOT paste those keys into action.
studio_composes_exactly: integrated_multimodal_description: SCENE – {title}. [Shot 1] {visual_style} Location: {location} Main character: {character} Action: {action} Camera: {camera} {character} (S1) says: <d>[{Lang}] {dialogue}</d> Constraints: {important}
h3_prompt_format.quality: Author fields must be DETAILED so the composed prompt is rich. Short generic beats (he walks, she looks) are rejected. Each action = 2-5 present-tense visible sentences for THIS beat only: body, hands, eyes, weather, props, light. Camera = size + lens feel + move + height (not just close-up). audio = diegetic room/Foley only. music = N/A unless the user asked for score.

_instructions.editor_fields: Fill the advanced reference, opening/ending frame, camera, transition and beats fields when applicable so the scene editor can display them; do not put them only inside action or camera prose.

shot_structure.principle: mode t2v = a CUT: a new camera setup (new angle or framing, new location, or a time jump). mode continue = the SAME shot still rolling: the camera may keep moving (push-in, follow, orbit, crane) but never jumps to a new framing or angle.
shot_structure.rhythm: Build the film from short unbroken pieces: one t2v section followed by 1-3 continue sections (10-20 s without a cut), then cut with the next t2v. Camera variety comes from the cuts, never from continue sections. A single t2v section without continues is fine for a quick insert.
shot_structure.location_change: A new location or time jump is ALWAYS t2v and starts a new chapter.
continue_rules: opening_frame = the previous section's ending_frame (same framing, same positions).
camera describes how the SAME shot keeps going (e.g. 'the slow push-in continues over his shoulder until the monitor fills the frame'); no new shot size, angle or lens.
action covers only the next seconds; do not re-describe the location, the wardrobe or who the character is.
location stays the same as the previous section.
shot_structure.one_shot_per_section: Each section is ONE shot. Never write 'cut to', 'cut-in', 'montage', 'multi-angle' or 'then a close-up of ...' inside a section; make it a new t2v section instead. One section (5 s) holds one or two visible actions.
shot_structure.mode_required: Write mode (t2v or continue) on EVERY section; Studio does not guess it.

example.camera: Wide shot from behind his left shoulder, slow push-in toward the monitor.
example.ending_frame: Over-the-shoulder medium shot, monitor glowing ahead of him.

example.camera: The push-in continues over his shoulder until his hands and the boss health bar fill the frame.
example.opening_frame: Over-the-shoulder medium shot, monitor glowing ahead of him.

example.camera: Cut to a side medium shot at desk height, static, as the screen freezes.
example.ending_frame: Side medium shot, his hands lifted off the keyboard.

final_checklist: Every section has mode t2v or continue. A camera angle change, new location or time jump is t2v.

Every continue section: same location as the previous section, opening_frame equals the previous ending_frame, camera describes the same shot still moving, action does not re-describe the place or character.
No section contains 'cut to', 'cut-in', 'montage' or several shots.
Every section has opening_frame and ending_frame filled.
sections.length equals the scene count; a new location starts a new chapter with a t2v section.
character and location use exact card names, spelled the same everywhere.
The story follows the human's scenario and scene count.
All visual fields are English; dialogue_lang matches the dialogue.
_instructions and _user are deleted; the answer is only valid JSON.

_user.READ_ME_HUMAN: Fill scenes + about here, or just write the scene count, topic and scenario in your chat message. Then send this WHOLE file to an AI.
_user.READ_ME_AI: The brief is in _user and/or the chat message (see _instructions.input_sources). Follow the human's scenario; invent only what is missing. Follow strict_section_contract and shot_structure exactly. Do not ask questions. Do not leave action/camera/audio blank, and explicitly fill character + location on every relevant section.
